q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
(a) **Time left until resolution**

Today is 2026-08-24. NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 was issued on May 20, 2026, with guidance of $91.0 billion ±2%. Q2 FY2027 would typically report in August-September 2026 (NVIDIA's fiscal calendar runs Feb-Jan), so we are currently very close to or possibly at the earnings report date itself. The resolution would occur when NVIDIA reports actual Q2 FY2027 results, likely within days to a few weeks from today. Time to resolution: **approximately 0-4 weeks**.

(b) **Most likely outcome and why**

The research provides NVIDIA's own forward guidance: **$91.0 billion ±2%**, which translates to a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion. This is the company's official guidance issued on May 20, 2026. Wall Street's consensus estimate is $91.9 billion, which sits comfortably within NVIDIA's guided range and just 1% above the midpoint.

Historically, large technology companies like NVIDIA tend to meet or slightly beat their own forward guidance, as they typically provide conservative estimates. Given that:
- NVIDIA explicitly provided this guidance range
- Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) falls within the range
- The guidance explicitly accounts for China data center restrictions
- NVIDIA has a strong track record of meeting guidance

The most likely outcome is that actual Q2 FY2027 revenue falls within or very close to the $89.2-$92.8 billion guidance range, with a central tendency around $91.0-$91.9 billion.

(c) **What would push the value lower?**

- Weaker-than-expected AI demand or data center spending slowdown
- Supply chain disruptions or manufacturing delays
- Market share losses to competitors (AMD, other AI chip makers)
- Macro economic weakness affecting customer capex spending
- Unexpected regulatory or geopolitical developments beyond the China restrictions already priced in
- Conservative execution or lower-than-expected product adoption

(d) **What would push the value higher?**

- Stronger-than-expected AI infrastructure demand exceeding NVIDIA's conservative guidance
- Faster-than-expected adoption of new product lines (Blackwell, etc.)
- Higher average selling prices (ASP) from premium product mix
- Accelerated hyperscaler and enterprise data center spending
- Upside from non-China regions offsetting any headwinds
- Market share gains from competitive advantages in AI

(e) **Base rate or historical reference values**

The research explicitly states that NVIDIA issued forward guidance of **$91.0 billion ±2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B) on May 20, 2026. This is the authoritative baseline for this forecast, as it is NVIDIA's own official guidance for the quarter in question. Wall Street consensus sits at $91.9 billion, approximately 1% above the midpoint and squarely within the company's range. No other historical base rate is needed—we have the company's own forward guidance.

---

**Analysis:**

This is a straightforward case where we have the company's actual forward guidance for the exact metric being asked. NVIDIA guided to $91.0B ±2% for Q2 FY2027 revenue. The question asks what NVIDIA's forward guidance *will be* in the earnings release, which has essentially already occurred (guidance was issued May 20, 2026, and it's now late August 2026—the report is imminent or may have just happened).

Given:
1. NVIDIA's official guidance: $89.2B–$92.8B
2. Wall Street consensus: $91.9B (within range, 1% above midpoint)
3. Large tech companies typically meet guidance with slight upside
4. Strong demand backdrop for AI infrastructure
5. Guidance already accounts for known constraints (China restrictions)

The most likely outcome is that actual results fall within or slightly above the guided range, centering around $91.0–$92.0 billion. I'll place my median estimate at $91.5 billion (midway between guidance midpoint and Wall Street consensus), with modest confidence that results stay within the $89–$93 billion band.

The 10th percentile accounts for meaningful demand miss scenarios, while the 90th percentile reflects potential for beating guidance through stronger-than-expected execution or demand.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). This implies a range from approximately $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The outlook explicitly excludes any data center compute revenue from China [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's provided guidance range, about 1% above the midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance still represents significant year-over-year growth, nearly doubling the $46.7 billion reported in the year-ago quarter [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
